record.question: The old man looked with caution before he crossed the busy street.
record.explanation: Answer A: cautiously before. “Looked cautiously before he crossed” uses the adverb cautiously to modify looked and preserves the intended temporal clause. Independent check: “Looked cautiously before he crossed” uses the adverb “cautiously” to modify looked; this is the clearest grammatical improvement among the options. Reference: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/adverbs. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Exact printed question, choices and required directions/emphasis reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.

record.questionMarkup: The old man looked <u>with caution before</u> he crossed the busy street.
